Name: Exploratory Research
Description: Early research on a topic that isn't well understood yet. It helps figure out what questions to ask and what to look at more closely.

Name: Field Research
Description: Collecting data by watching or talking to people in their real setting, like a workplace, classroom or neighborhood, instead of a lab.

Name: Market Research
Description: Research about customers and markets: what people want, what they would buy, and how they see a product or its competitors.

Name: Randomized Controlled Trial
Description: Randomly splits people into groups, changes something for one group, and compares the results. The strongest way to test if something actually causes an effect.

Name: Policy Research
Description: Studies how laws, rules or programs work and what effects they have, to help decision makers choose or improve a policy.

Name: Systematic Review
Description: Gathers and evaluates all the existing studies on a question with a clear, repeatable process, to sum up what the evidence says overall.

Name: Product R&D
Description: Research and development to design, build and test a new product, or improve an existing one, before it launches.
Also Called: Product Research and Development; Product; ProductResearchAndDevelopment

Name: Longitudinal Research
Description: Studies the same people or things again and again over a long time to see how they change.
